utterances.text: Meaning then from those two facts that it was the Muslims who were the biggest losers under the Vance-Owen Plan, correct?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO VUCINA
utterances.text: I think they and we too. But if we talked about nuances then, I think it's quite evident that the Muslims were most affected by the Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me turn to a completely different subject, sir, and that is the issue of -- forgive me, Your Honour, just keep my notes straight. That's the issue of Mr. Kordic being given this title of colonel. You say in your statement and you've testified today that you were, yourself, directly involved in the events leading or -- leading to or involving the creation of this title or rank of colonel given to Mr. Kordic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO VUCINA
utterances.text: Correct, alongside Mr. Bozo Rajic, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you recall being told? You said you had a conversation with Mr. Kordic personally. What do you recall being told about this UNPROFOR requirement that the participants in the military -- the mixed military working group had to have military rank?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO VUCINA
utterances.text: I did not speak about the requirements nor do I know anything about requirements. But during the conversation, we realised that it was necessary, in such a broad group, to have certain weight and that it would be best to have such an honourary title so as to command respect in these talks. That is the only reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, you say in paragraph 17, you say he was given the rank so he could attend a mixed military working group in Sarajevo and the way you've stated there, sir, that rank was a pre-requisite for someone before he could participate in those meetings?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO VUCINA
utterances.text: I doubt that that is what I stated, and particularly that that was some kind of a condition for participation in talks, and such interpretation of my statement, now it is not like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, we'll leave the statement. It speaks for itself. I won't belabour it for the moment. But you understood that for some reason, someone, Mr. Kordic wanted to be given a rank of colonel and you and Mr. Boban and Mr. Stojic were -- made a decision that yes, in fact, we will call Mr. Kordic a colonel; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO VUCINA
utterances.text: I think it was based on our conversations between me and Mr. Bozo Rajic's that there was such a request. I can't really remember that nor am I sure that there was such a request.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you say, sir, you've told us that you were personally involved. This was not something that you heard about but this is something that you had hands-on involvement in; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO VUCINA
utterances.text: It is. We judged that it was necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You judged that it was necessary, all right. And then what did you personally do to make this happen, that he would be given this rank of colonel?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO VUCINA
utterances.text: Mr. Bozo Rajic was due to contact Mr. President as one of the vice-presidents and said that we were recommending Mr. President to do accordingly, and that is all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, this mixed military working group process, these series of meetings, this was very important, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO VUCINA
utterances.text: I'm not fully informed about it so even with the best of will, I cannot really say, but it was important, with regard to what they were doing, in the sense of the functioning of life in those areas in general. One should no doubt appreciate the efforts made by that group and results which I believe they achieved in that regard. That was a major effort of the police forces and --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My only question was this was something significant, this wasn't something trivial, was it?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO VUCINA
utterances.text: I am not a person who can say yes or no, but if one looks at the results, it is quite obvious that for life that existed in those areas, it was important to function every day, so the answer is yes. I doubt that there was another group which was as important for the functioning of life under the wartime conditions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as part of that or all of that group's business, it was military business, wasn't it? That's why it was called the mixed military working group.

utterances.speaker: SRECKO VUCINA
utterances.text: I did not take part it in, and apart from what I have said, I did not take part in its work directly so that I cannot really judge whether it was exclusively but I do not think that it was exclusively military, because if it were, there would have been one of the commanders from the Main Staff. As it was the case in some other talks, when General Petkovic personally conducted the talks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vucina, you were -- Mr. Boban, you've told us, was the commander in chief; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO VUCINA
utterances.text: Correct. That was according to the organisation of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mr. Boban had complete authority by his own hand to name anyone to a high military position or rank; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO VUCINA
utterances.text: Yes, by standard and especially in the case of high ranks, he had the sole competence to accord ranks. Sometimes the head of a department would nominate somebody and the president would then decide yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Boban could confer military power on whoever he wanted to, couldn't he?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO VUCINA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in the conditions required by the regulations on the organisation of the Croat Defense Council for the active part. For instance, he could not do it in the active part, confer them on me who had no qualifications or someone else so someone would tell between active officers and others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went on this morning for some time and this early afternoon that Mr. Boban had almost extreme exhaustive authority. In fact, in some respects, your testimony would indicate that he was the only person who had authority. Is it correct that, in fact, Mr. Boban could confer military authority on anyone he chose to confer it on?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO VUCINA
utterances.text: As I said this morning, what I said in my summary and I confirm that with regard to the powers, competencies, and the authority of Mr. Boban, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said in paragraph 23, he was clearly the supreme commanders of the armed forces he exercised that authority by appointing people and signing the necessary documents. So, sir, if Mr. Boban wanted to confer military power on Mr. Kordic, he could do so at any time, couldn't he?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO VUCINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, it's a few minutes to 4.00 and it's time for us to adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, as the Court may have the sense of I apologise but can I not complete this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Would you look to do it please in a quarter of an hour or so tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'll try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Because we have a lot to get through tomorrow. What we shall do is this, we'll sit at 9.00 to deal with the matters of law when Judge Bennouna will be present. So we won't start on the witness, I would anticipate before half past nine. What we haven't got or I haven't seen is the Prosecution's submissions about the witness, and also about the affidavits and I would be grateful to have those.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The submissions about the witness were distributed informally yesterday notwithstanding the fact that they were filed yesterday afternoon and early in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: They haven't found their way to us. It's most important that we have them. I gather there are no informal copies. It may be helpful if we could have some informal copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think your legal officer probably has them, but we'll sort it out with her in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, we have must have them tonight.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: As for the affidavits, as soon as the document is ready, I'll make it available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. President, in fairness to Mr. Nice, he did distribute a copy of his submission to us yesterday and we've prepared a response to that which I have here for the Court's information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you had alike to hand it in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, Judge Robinson apparently has the Prosecution's submissions. He has the advantage over me. Mr. Vucina, would you be back, please, tomorrow morning at half past nine to conclude your evidence? We have, in fact, some other administrative matters and legal matters to deal with first, but we'll try and get to your evidence as soon after half past nine as possible. So if you would be back then, please. We'll sit at 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: at 4.02 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 9th day of June, 2000, at 9 a.m.
